children: BT Group's first-half results suggest its plans for cost cuts are intact as it completes the roll-out of fiber broadband, while dividend payments could rise, Berenberg analysts write. The telecommunication company's consumer earnings were better than expected, with overall revenue above expectations, the analysts note. The company maintains its fiscal 2027 and 2030 cash flow guidance, which implies cost cuts will continue as expected, Berenberg says. The company also makes positive comments that suggest a rise in dividend payouts is possible once its balance sheet position improves, the analysts note. BT's new pension terms allow substantial upside to its dividend after targets are met, the analysts add. Shares are up 5.4%. (michael.hennessey@wsj.com)
